newsitem.title: USA: Carlton makes investment in Getty.
newsitem.headline: Carlton makes investment in Getty.

text.p: Getty Communications Plc said Tuesday that Carlton Communications had invested about $28.5 million in Getty through a subscription for 3.7 million Class A ordinary shares, or about 1.9 million ADRs.
Carlton will own 10 percent of Getty and has the right to increase its holding to 20 percent within two years, Getty said.
Getty said it expects operational and strategic benefits to flow from closer cooperation with Carlton.

As part of the same deal, Getty Investments LLC, the controlling shareholder of Getty, exercised an option at the same price as the Carlton deal. Getty Investments subscribed for about 2.1 million Class B shares for $16.0 million, the company said.

Getty also said it was mulling various acquisition opportunities, including image collections to companies that provide contemporary stock and archival photography, as well as news, current affairs, features and celebrity material.
Getty also plans several operational changes to improve the efficiency of its picture research and sales operations in the United Kingdom and the United States.
In the U.S., Getty's Los Angeles and Seattle offices will be merged with its operations in Chicago.
In the UK, Getty will merge various functions of Tony Stone Images and Hulton Getty in order to better coordinate image scanning and administrative functions.
The company declined comment on the expected cost savings from these efforts.
